description: Microsoft publishes no company-defined capex figure in SEC filings or SEC-furnished releases; its quoted "capital expenditures including finance leases" appears only on calls and in investor materials.
likely_explanation: Microsoft reports cash additions to property and equipment in its statements and quotes a broader measure on calls.
recommended_treatment: Series A for Microsoft = NOT FOUND in stage 1; the race uses cash additions to property and equipment (series B), as for the other US companies.

description: Amazon's gross cash purchases of property and equipment are printed only from 2017 (FY2017 10-K and 2018 10-Qs); before that the single printed line is net of property and equipment incentives.
likely_explanation: Amazon re-presented its statement from the FY2017 10-K.
recommended_treatment: Race uses Amazon's net figure (its own capex measure, continuous 2009-2026); the other US companies are gross. Net is lower than gross by Amazon's incentives (2017: 13% of gross).

description: Meta's own capex measure adds principal payments on finance leases from Q1 2019 (ASC 842); from 2022 it deducts proceeds relating to property and equipment.
likely_explanation: Change of the company's measure, not a restatement.
recommended_treatment: Series A is kept but not used for the race; the race uses cash purchases of P&E as printed in the statement.

description: Meta's cash-flow statement prints "Purchases of property and equipment, net" (net of proceeds) from its 2024 filings, re-presenting 2023.
likely_explanation: Presentation change; proceeds were 0-2% of purchases.
recommended_treatment: Quarters use the figures as first reported; TTM windows spanning 2023-2024 are flagged definition_break_in_TTM.

description: Six quarters printed as "capital expenditures and (acquisition of) intangible assets" (Mar 2017-Mar 2018) and "... and licensed copyrights" (Jun 2018): broader than Alibaba's capex before and after.
source_2: Alibaba releases before 2017 and from Sep 2018
value_2: PP&E incl. land use rights and CIP
likely_explanation: Alibaba changed what it called capital expenditure; no quarterly bridge was found.
recommended_treatment: DEFINITION_BREAK in H; not spliced; Alibaba has no TTM point from 2017 Q1 to 2019 Q1 buckets.

description: No group-level quarterly capex before the quarter ended 30 Jun 2013 (pre-IPO). The March 2013 quarter could only be built component by component from the F-1; not done in stage 1.
recommended_treatment: NOT_FOUND; Alibaba enters the race at the quarter ended March 2014 (bucket 2014 Q1).

description: No quarterly capex figure printed for 2009-2010; 2011 quarters exist only as comparatives in 2012 announcements.

description: Tencent's capex is ADDITIONS (accrual) to PP&E, construction in progress, land use rights, investment properties (from Q3 2017) and intangible assets excluding content licences - not cash purchases of property and equipment.
likely_explanation: Different measure; Tencent prints cash purchases of PP&E only half-yearly.
recommended_treatment: Shown with a definition warning or excluded: question for Luke.

description: Sharadar SF1 capex (8 Aug 2026 download) compared quarter by quarter. Equal to our figures: Amazon 69 of 69 (Amazon net series), Microsoft 69 of 69, Oracle 67 of 69, Meta 50 of 58, Alphabet 39 of 69. Differences: Meta 2022-2023 (vendor nets proceeds, the filing printed gross at the time); Alphabet 2016-2019 (under 1%: vendor uses later re-presented values); Alphabet 2009-2015 and Oracle Q3-Q4 FY2011 (vendor values do not match the filings; e.g. 2014 Q1 Google's own release prints $2,345m, as we do). Alibaba: vendor quarterly capex blank/zero, annual within 1-3% of Alibaba's printed capex; Baidu: no vendor capex.
likely_explanation: Vendor definition: purchases of PP&E net of disposal proceeds (empirically; vendor documentation site blocked).
recommended_treatment: Vendor never overwrites a filing value; full comparison only in the private repo (research/rtt-103/build/sharadar_crosscheck_private.csv).
